column6: SHIP-WITH-FIX, and the fix is handed to the in-flight pitflip round to avoid contending for the same file. SIX SEATS SOUND, CODEX DEFECTIVE -- and codex was RIGHT: "the latch is never consumed, so the selected counter returns zero indefinitely." VERIFIED IN SOURCE: latched[] is SET at :212, cleared ONLY at :219 by a non-latch mode write, and NEVER cleared by the read at :163. So after one latch command every subsequent read of that counter returns 0 until the guest happens to rewrite the mode byte. A real 8254 CONSUMES the latch per the programmed RW format. NOT a regression -- pre-#439 a latch clobbered mode_byte and subsequent reads also fell to the default arm returning 0, plus an unsilenceable flood -- but a real defect in the fix, found by the one seat that had been walled for the pass-1 panel. glm gestured at the same thing ("the sticky latch"). THE CONSUME SEMANTICS INTERACT WITH THE LSB/MSB FLIP-FLOP: in 16-bit mode a real latch delivers TWO bytes before reverting, which is precisely the selector pitflip is fixing -- so the fix belongs in that round, with a named detector row that latches, reads twice, and asserts the second read is not still 0. The six SOUND verdicts converged on the substantive question the brief asked -- agy: "returning 0 avoids guest kernel divide-by-zero crashes, preserves programmed mode state"; deepseek: "the least harmful of three wrong answers and not a guest-visible regression"; minimax: "the write-side fix matches the 8254 and removes a real bug". So the refusal of the pass-1 majority is VINDICATED by pass 2, and the shipped shape stands; what was missed was the consume.

column6: SHIP-WITH-CHANGES, applied in the same commit. *** SEVEN OF EIGHT SEATS SAID SHIP, AND THE 9-ROW DETECTOR THEY WERE APPROVING PASSED SIX MUTANTS. ***  The single dissent was the one seat that COMPILED AND RAN, and the sharpest of its six puts exit(1) BACK on a guest-reachable path -- the round's headline property -- with every row green: 'if (partial && writeflag == MEM_READ) exit(1);', measured to end the process on one mov.b. Root cause structural, not careless: reachable shapes are (read|write) x len(1|2|4) = SIX and the detector exercised FIVE -- no row did a 1-byte READ. Two more (delete BCR2's mask, add one to BCR3) escaped because BOTH write oracles were MASK-TRANSPARENT -- D1 wrote 0x89ab3ffd and 0x3ffd & 0x3ffd is 0x3ffd, so a row NAMED 'masked' could not see the mask. One constant (0xc003 -> 0x0001) kills both. A fourth neutered the whole big-endian lane, a fifth swapped the Ignored/Servicing ternary so the diagnostic stated the opposite of what happened. Detector 9 -> 13 rows; pre-fix 2/13; every mutant now killed by a named row; clean tree 13/13. *** THE READING SEATS EARNED THEIR PLACE ON THE SAME QUESTION: agy INDEPENDENTLY FOUND THE BIG-ENDIAN MUTANT BY READING ALONE (replace sh4_bsc16_shift's body with 'return 0;'), and codex reached the same requirement -- 'cover the big-endian 4-byte lane behavior; the code itself does not need a functional change.' ***  Reading seat named the family, measuring seat proved the instance. Codex also named a residual nobody else did: the latch keys on SITE, so a byte read can demote a later 4-byte write's first report -- consistent with the stated policy, so recorded not fixed. FOUR OF THE ROUND'S OWN ERRORS WERE CAUGHT BY RUNS, NOT REASONING: (1) the first version of the fix WAS mutant M1 -- the helper returned 1 unconditionally so a 1-byte write overwrote the whole register with 0xa5, and D3 caught it, a row a pass-1 seat had written against exactly that; (2) D4's first version ran the two sites in SEPARATE PROCESSES, so the shared-latch mutant passed 9/9 -- each fresh process starts with both flags clear, and the file's own docstring said 'in ONE process' while the code did not; (3) MY POSITIVE CONTROL PASSED 12/12, and assuming a dead pipeline would have buried a real hole -- neutering the len==2 fast path makes every LEGAL 16-bit driver access emit a complaint -q cannot silence, now pinned by D10, and five other mutants died in the same run so the pipeline was demonstrably alive; (4) D7b's expected constant was lifted from another probe with a different input, and its first input discriminated by one bit. TWO WRONG RECORDS IN MY OWN COMMENTS, measured false by the pass-2 seat: the len<2 guard's comment shouted that a 1-byte store is 'reachable -- measured' when the store is reachable but the FUNCTION is not reached with it (traced across all twelve report-calls); and the header comment argued against dropping a write while the code dropped one, invisibly so free-running because debug() computes v = verbose - 1 = -1 and returns. Both corrected to say what the code does. A FACTUAL ERROR IN MY PASS-1 BRIEF gave the cleanest test of the seat-class doctrine this project has: I asserted BCR3 is at 0xff800006 without opening sh4_bscreg.h:70, where it reads 0xff800050. EVERY SEAT THAT COULD OPEN THE HEADER CAUGHT IT (agy, kimi, grok); EVERY PACKET-FED SEAT BUILT ON IT, two producing whole designs around the imagined adjacency. Codex could have opened it and did not -- 'cannot check' and 'did not check' are different failures. '_mark' is the idiom in every other pty probe. Filed as sh4markspell. Gates: gate_hygiene PASS (48), gate_offline PASS (259), each run singly. column6: SHIP-WITH-CHANGES, applied before this receipt was filed. *** THE ROUND HAD SHIPPED WITH NO PASS 2 AT ALL -- and with no CHANGELOG block, and a ledger row still reading state=held / commits="" / 'no fix exists yet' a day after the commit. The precommit gate refused the NEXT commit with 'NO PASS-2 RECEIPT for 3193d56', which is how it was caught; section F did exactly what it was built for and the round would otherwise have passed unreviewed. *** 8 seats fired, 7/7 scriptable answered (codex SHIP, agy SHIP, kimi SHIP 117 KB, grok SHIP WITH CHANGES, glm/deepseek SHIP, minimax SHIP WITH CHANGES) plus the opus5 measuring seat; fable5 DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED per the owner's standing deprioritisation, recorded as a deliberate omission and never as agreement. *** THE MEASURING SEAT BUILT TWELVE MUTANTS AND FIVE PASSED BOTH DETECTORS; EIGHT PASSED THE ONLY DETECTOR ANY GATE ACTUALLY RUNS. ***  The smallest is ONE TOKEN: `double bound = freq;` -> `double bound = freq / 100.0;`. At a 0.5 s accrual the shipped build owes the guest 375 interrupts and that mutant delivers FOUR -- 99% of the guest's clock destroyed, both detectors green. That is precisely the failure timer.h's 'THE BACKLOG IS RETAINED' paragraph exists to prevent. THE CAUSE WAS STRUCTURAL: R1 asserted worst_peak <= ceiling, an inequality against a CONSTANT. It computed the case's own rate `f`, PRINTED it, and compared nothing to it -- so any bound between R0's floor (4096) and the ceiling (68,157,440) satisfied it, and any bound at all satisfied the low side. CLOSED BY TWO ROWS NEEDING NO NEW ORACLE, since `f` was already computed for the message: R5 makes it an EQUALITY against the timer's own rate (kills freq/100 on 6 rows and bound-is-ceiling on 5), and R6/R6b re-arm a timer at a DIFFERENT rate and require each timer's bound to track its own (kills bound-frozen-after-first-arm and [0]-instead-of-[nr]). R6 exists because the case table ARMS ALL FOUR TIMERS WITH IDENTICAL PARAMETERS AND ARMS EACH EXACTLY ONCE, so it was structurally blind to both. Re-measured after adding them: freq/100 -> R5, bound-frozen -> R6, bound-is-ceiling -> both. The floor-deleted mutant still passes and CORRECTLY so -- byte-identical, an equivalent mutant rather than a survivor. FOUR COMMENTS IN THE SHIPPED CODE MEASURED FALSE, all corrected: (1) the clamp claimed to match timer_clamp_freq's NaN idiom and is THE INVERSE -- timer.c:80-82 puts the floor first deliberately 'so a NaN lands SLOW rather than fast' and this tested the ceiling first (harmless, NaN is unreachable: emulated_hz is an int and footbridge_effective_cycles is >= 1 by construction); (2) the floor's stated reason is false -- with it present the slowest case already reads peak 1, with it deleted the output is BYTE-IDENTICAL; (3) the ordering comment called itself load-bearing and is not -- moving the store below the switch is a ZERO-BYTE object delta passing every row, and it is redundant with the DEVINIT seed which no comment mentioned; (4) *** THE DEVINIT SEED USED THE WRONG CONSTANT *** -- it seeded the CEILING and called that 'the safe default', but at cats' 762.94 Hz the ceiling is TWENTY-FIVE HOURS of un-acked backlog and a mutant seeding it reads 3051 on the drain probe, indistinguishable from pre-fix. Now 1. A NUMBER FILED TWICE THAT THE FIX MAKES ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the commit message and OUTSTANDING_BUGS both said '2772 pending after 46 s even with #442 shipped'. The bound is 762; the counter cannot exceed it. MEASURED on the shipped build: 100. The clause after it -- 'because #442 bounds the rate and not a legitimately accrued debt' -- is backwards, since pending_timer_interrupts IS the accrued debt and #442 bounds exactly that. A pre-fix projection carried into a post-fix sentence without re-measuring; corrected in the bug file and the ledger, with the same caution applied to fbdisabled's own pre-fix 3051 (shipped reads 3). The drain probe's docstring claimed 'post-fix it is the cap' -- also false: once the bound is first reached the number is a MODULAR RESIDUE of the delivered tick count (3 at 4 s, 100 at 46 s, 375 at 0.5 s, one binary, one bound), which is why --expect-cap is one-sided and cannot tell a bound of 762 from one of 7. THE WITNESS IS NOW COMMITTED as regress/fbpending_witness.py -- it lived in _scratchpad/, so a clone could not re-run the reproduction that licensed the fix (the mrwstore2 shape, whose probe left no artefact at all). Gate 6 EXPECT_CONVERTED 20 -> 21, all three counts moving together. STILL OPEN AND DECLARED: nothing runs fbpending_drain_probe.py -- gate_offline says so in a comment and gate_hygiene only COUNTS it -- and its assertion is opt-in, so wiring it in without --expect-cap would be born vacuous. Filed rather than fixed: choosing that flag's value is choosing what the row asserts, and R5/R6 now pin the property it was reaching for. column6: SHIP-WITH-CHANGES, applied before this receipt. *** SEVEN MUTANTS ALL SCORED 29/29 AGAINST THE SHIPPED DETECTOR *** -- three guest-visible, one reinstating the original host kill verbatim: killw (`if (len == 2) exit(1);`), restinlatch (the restore braced INSIDE the latch, re-opening corruption on the second offence at all ten arms), nombrrestore (one restore deleted), bothvoid (both void PCICONF0 statements deleted -- LEAKS GUEST DATA), plus three void or equivalent mutants. *** AND THE ROUND HAD DISCLOSED ONE HOLE WITHOUT READING IT: its own kill table says 'the restores deleted -> 27/29, P3 and P3b, AND NOTHING ELSE', which is the statement that ONLY 2 OF THE 10 RESTORES ARE COVERED. I wrote that line as a strength. *** BOTH CAUSES WERE STRUCTURAL. The 274-access census was ONE-DIMENSIONAL -- an instrumented build reports widths seen: ['4'], so 137 offsets x 2 directions x ONE width, and len=2 was never issued anywhere in the file although a 16-bit access reaches the device. And the two void statements are MUTUALLY MASKING, so single-line mutation cannot see either while deleting both leaks the guest's word. DETECTOR 29 -> 38 ROWS and every mutant now dies: killw -> P14/P14b (len=2 census); restinlatch -> P17/P18 (second offence); nombrrestore -> P16/P17 (first offence parameterised over all 8 guarded arms); bothvoid -> P19 (-C SH7750 write-then-read); perofflatch -> P20. NO NEW ROW IS VACUOUS -- each of the nine kills something -- and restinlatch leaving P16 GREEN is the useful negative: the first offence really is still restored, so P17 is a distinct defect rather than a duplicate. Two extra controls came with it: noconf6restore proves P16 is parameterised rather than PCIMBR-specific, and killb_narrow is the DISCRIMINATING control for P15, since plain killb was already caught by the old file and so could not isolate the len=1 census. *** A REAL DEFECT IN THE SHIPPED CODE, AND MY FIRST FIX FOR IT WAS HALF A FIX. ***  The latch merged semantically DIFFERENT faults at one offset -- the exact hazard the code's own comment claimed to avoid, one level below #438's '1 of 4 kinds'. Measured twice: with -C SH7750 a write to PCICONF0 suppressed the later 'read for unimplemented CPU type' (which DOES print in a fresh process), and a byte-write at 0xfe200015 suppressed the later 'PCICONF5 unknown value', because PCIC_REG() maps both addresses to one word. I added TWO fault classes; the seat then measured that as HALF A FIX -- it closed the aliasing case and left PCICONF0 open, because BOTH of that register's complaints were BADVAL at the same word index and still shared one bit. A THIRD class fixes it, and the lesson outlives the fix: THE CLASSES ARE KINDS OF COMPLAINT, NOT KINDS OF REGISTER, and one register can raise several -- counting them from the register's point of view is what produced the half-fix. Severity throughout was diagnostic-only because the restore sits OUTSIDE the `if` and state stayed correct -- and THAT PLACEMENT IS LOAD-BEARING, which is exactly what restinlatch proves: bracing it inside is a brace slip of the kind a tidy-up produces. Gate 10's row floor 29 -> 38 in the same edit that grew the probe. It is a FLOOR, so it would have stayed green at 38 with no edit at all -- which is how a floor stops noticing. STILL OPEN AND DECLARED, filed as pcicmergeA: reproduction A (the PCICONF0 merge) has no row. It COULD NOT have had one at the time -- writing it against the two-class code would have CEMENTED THE DEFECT, asserting the merged behaviour as correct, so a later correct fix would have looked like a regression. The seat named that and declined rather than writing a row that passed. The third class now exists, so the row is three lines, and it is filed rather than written because it needs a probe run made AFTER that class landed. Also unmeasured: whether a real landisk boot ever issues a narrow-width PCIC access, so P14/P15 are rung-3 reachability rather than boot knowledge; and whether the guest driver ever commits a second offence at one register, so P17/P18 assert the contract rather than driver behaviour. Gates: gate 10 PASS (52), gate_offline PASS (263), gate_hygiene PASS (48), each run singly.

A field-by-field row set would have had exactly the shape that just failed. column6: SHIP THE FIX, REPLACE THE DETECTOR -- and the detector was replaced before this receipt was filed. 8 seats fired, 7of7 scriptable answered (codex, agy, kimi 69KB, grok, glm, deepseek, minimax) plus the opus5 measuring seat; fable5 DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED per the owner's standing deprioritisation, recorded as a deliberate omission and never as agreement. SIX of the seven returned DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR; minimax said SOUND-with-the-detector-as-the-weaker-link, which is the same finding under a different label. *** THE MEASURING SEAT BUILT SIXTEEN MUTANTS AND ALL SIXTEEN SCORED 7/7. *** The champion is TWO CHARACTERS: `ETHERNET_STRING_MAXLEN` -> `0*ETHERNET_STRING_MAXLEN`. snprintf with size 0 writes NOTHING, not even the NUL, so the heap-buffer-overflow returns on ip12/ip28/ip30/ip35 -- ASan-measured back to the pre-fix numbers -- and it compiles with ZERO warnings while the gate row printed green. Also 7/7: size 1 (writes only the NUL -> EMPTY MAC, ASan silent), sizeof(eaddr_string) (=8 -> "08:20:3"), `#if 0`, a comment wrapper, `if (0)`, `if (subtype == 32)`, a second malloc, an arm re-pointing the pointer, and `#define snprintf(b,l,...) ((void)(b))`. *** AND THE REDUCTIO THAT SETTLES IT: A 217-BYTE FILE CONTAINING NOTHING BUT A C COMMENT SCORED 7/7. *** No function, no MACHINE_SETUP, nothing compilable. That is VACUOUS under this project's taxonomy, not weak -- and no additional regex repairs it, because the failure is the MEDIUM and not the rows. THE OLD FILE'S OWN STATED PURPOSE WAS THE THING IT DID NOT DO. Its docstring called itself "the LENGTH/FORMAT oracle" that sees what ASan cannot. IT NEVER EXAMINED THE LENGTH ARGUMENT. The size-1 mutant is precisely the `eaddr_string[0]='\0'` hole it named as its reason for existing, spelled with an snprintf, and it passed. Three tracked copies of that claim (probe docstring, CHANGELOG, gate comment) were corrected under the grep-for-siblings rule. REPLACED WITH A RUNTIME VALUE ORACLE, 10 rows: break on arcbios_init() in a real construction of the five reaching subtypes and require the ethernet STRING to be the formatting of the MAC BYTES passed beside it -- a provenance check, so garbage, empty, truncated and right-shaped-wrong-octet all fail. MEASURED kill table (PASSING rows out of 10; clean = 10/10): `0*` 5/10, size-1 5/10, sizeof 5/10, `#if 0` 5/10, comment 5/10, pre-fix 5/10, wrong-last-octet 6/10. Every mutant that beat the old file dies. *** V4 KILLED NOTHING IN THAT TABLE AND THAT WAS CORRECT, SO A DISCRIMINATING MUTANT WAS BUILT FOR IT. *** ip32 has its own snprintf in its arm and is rescued from every mutation of the pre-switch fill. An untested row is indistinguishable from a vacuous one, so both fills were removed: 4/10, V4 fires. No row now goes unexercised. GATE MOVED, AND THE MOVE IS THE POINT: the old detector lived in gate_offline because source text needs no binary. The replacement needs build/gxemul and gdb, and gate_offline RUNS NO EMULATOR AT ALL (zero references to the binary) -- adding one would have made the gate's own name untrue. It went to gate 9, which already constructs every machine and subtype: ASan is that gate's instrument for the memory-safety class, this probe is its instrument for the VALUE class ASan cannot see. check_probe_wiring.py followed the move with no edit, because it DERIVES wiring from run.sh's GATES array rather than asserting it. Nothing was left behind in gate_offline: a stub row asserting the probe merely EXISTS cannot fail for the reason it names. degrade() not gate_skip() on a missing gdb -- gate_skip EXITS and would have discarded the sweep's own eleven checks and reported the whole gate as SKIP. THREE WRONG RECORDS FOUND IN MY OWN MATERIAL, all corrected. (1) The `:633` citation had drifted to :661 -- the read-the-line-before-citing-it rule. (2) The added source comment said "machine.c forces machine->bootarg non-NULL"; machine.c:559 is a DEBUG PRINT whose local has_bootarg only selects which message is emitted, and bootarg is not on this path at all. The CONCLUSION (only defective caller) survives on the two-caller grep, which agy and grok both performed independently; the argument for it did not. (3) "callee-side hardening is an IMPOSSIBILITY" overreached: impossible AT THAT SIGNATURE, not categorically. *** THE UBSAN FOLLOW-UP UNDERCOUNTED ITSELF BY FIVE TIMES. *** It was filed as "two left-shift defects at arcbios.c:737/784". The measuring seat found ip32 never reaches those lines -- its two hits are :570 and :590 -- making it four sites. A grep for the idiom then found TEN unguarded `(buf[3]<<24)` sites and FOUR correctly cast `((uint32_t)buf[3]<<24)`. Line 580 sits BETWEEN 570 and 590 and is the only one of the three that is cast: the author knew the idiom and applied it to 4 of 14 sites. :737 is the damaging one -- the sign-extended low word is ADDED to high-word terms, so the 64-bit pointer's high word comes out off by one for every address with bit 31 set. A SEAT'S FACTUAL CHALLENGE WAS REFUTED BY EXECUTION WHILE ITS MECHANISM CLAIM WAS SIMULTANEOUSLY RIGHT. grok read the arms and reported ip27 has no abort(), so "five call abort()" overstates. MEASURED over all ten advertised subtypes: ip19/20/22/24/27 return 134 and ip12/28/30/32/35 return 1 -- the five ARE the five. But ip22 has no body and FALLS THROUGH into case 24, and ip27 dies under gdb at interrupt_handler_lookup() <- devinit_z8530() <- device_add(), on its own arm's irq=0 -- which is exactly what grok predicted. A token search of a switch cannot see fall-through, and reading for abort() misses an abort raised by a callee; my own case-splitter had the identical blind spot. kimi audited the kill-table ARITHMETIC rather than the code and challenged "four-octet MAC 6/7 (E5 alone)" as inconsistent. MEASURED: format-only mutant 6/7 with E5 the sole failure; format-AND-arguments mutant 5/7 with E5 and E6. Both numbers right, different mutants -- and the real defect it exposed is that "(E5 alone)" never says whether E5 alone FIRED or alone SURVIVED, and the two readings are opposite. A kill-table cell must name the direction. STILL OPEN AND DECLARED: the ip32 arm's own snprintf is now redundant; kept, because deleting it drops the buffer to a single write site and costs nothing to leave. Nothing here claims anything about the bytes the GUEST reads back -- that needs a rung-3 probe on a machine that gets that far, and there is no SGI rig. The probe reads arguments from SysV AMD64 registers because build/gxemul has no DWARF; that ties it to one ABI, stated in the file rather than hidden, with V6/V7 as the rows that would catch a wrong register rather than let it read as zero. Gates: gate_offline PASS (263), gate_asan_sweep PASS (13, was 11), each run singly.

column6: SHIP, WITH THE DETECTOR GAP FILED AND NAMED IN THE ROUND'S OWN CHANGELOG BLOCK. 8 seats fired, 7of7 scriptable answered (codex 19.5KB, agy 9KB, kimi 84KB, grok 6.4KB, glm 9KB, deepseek 2.5KB, minimax 8.5KB) plus the opus5 measuring seat; fable5 DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED per the owner's standing deprioritisation, recorded as a deliberate omission and never as agreement. Verdicts split 4 SOUND / 2 DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR / 1 format-miss, AND THE SPLIT DECIDED NOTHING -- the measuring seat built the mutants the reading seats could only predict. *** NINE MUTANTS SCORE 33/33, SEVEN OF THEM MEASURED REAL DEFECTS, ONE A GUEST-REACHABLE HOST DEATH. *** Smallest is ONE IDENTIFIER: `| TCR_UNIE` added to TCR_UNIMPLEMENTED. On the fix, TCR0=0x0022 reads back 0x22 with a clock line at 520833.328125 Hz; with the mutant it reads back 0x00000000 and there is NO clock line, and since TCR_UNIE is modelled the guest can never enable the timer interrupt. Worst is `if (timer_nr == 2 && len == 4) exit(1);` -- a mov.l to TCR2 gives alive=False, and it SURVIVES because len 2 is the only width the census issues. TWO SEATS FOUND THE SAME ONE-IDENTIFIER ESCAPE BY OPPOSITE METHODS -- opus5 by compiling and measuring, grok by reading without building. That convergence is the strongest signal this panel produced, and it is the reading-seat-buys-the-class / measuring-seat-buys-the-instance rule with both halves landing on one instance. FOUR STRUCTURAL HOLES, a PRODUCT rather than a list: state read back at INSTANCE 0 only (V11/V12 walk the others but only COUNT lines); read back on a FIRST offence only except at RCR1, where V18 exists for exactly that shape and its sibling was never added at TCR or DMATCR; masks pinned only FROM BELOW; width x instance covered only on the DIAGONAL. *** THE FIX CHANGED ONE HOLE'S FAILURE MODE FROM LOUD TO SILENT, AND THAT IS THE FINDING INSIDE THE FINDING. *** Pre-fix a widened guard mask meant exit(1) on a legal write -- unmissable. Post-fix it means a silently refused write. The round improved the failure and degraded its own detectability in the same edit, and NO RULE IN THIS HARNESS WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THAT. FILED AS sh4valrows RATHER THAN FIXED IN-ROUND, on a distinction this project has now made twice: #446's detector was VACUOUS (a 217-byte comment-only file passed it) and was replaced in-round; this one is WEAK -- it kills 25 of 33 rows pre-fix and kills six real mutants. The stopping rule (a MEASURED FALSE PASS is fixed in-round) and the reopening rule (more witnesses make more ROUNDS, not bigger rounds) point OPPOSITE WAYS here, so the call is queued for the flagship seat to adjudicate rather than settled by the author. CODEX'S CONTRIBUTION WAS AN HONEST REFUSAL THAT BECAME THE SHARPEST OPEN QUESTION. It declined to name a survivor -- 'I cannot honestly claim that edit still scores 33/33' -- because the packet never said WHICH bit the existing mask mutant removed. What it asked for is the quantifier-collapse shape: V28 writes all six unimplemented TCR bits AS A UNION, so deleting one leaves V28 green while a SINGLETON write of that bit reaches the prescaler and the store. UNSETTLED, and recorded as unsettled: it needs the fourteen mask-minus-one-bit mutants. Note it is a DIFFERENT test from pinning the mask from above, and both are wanted. GROK ALSO CORRECTED A SENTENCE IN MY OWN BRIEF: 'zero uint64_t declarations in cpu_sh_instr.c' is FALSE -- there are many; what is true is that none is a `uint64_t data` passed to memory_rw. Conclusion survived, supporting sentence did not. And it found an asymmetry no other seat had: narrowing the DMATCR guard by ONE NIBBLE stores bit 26, while sh4_dmac_transfer consumes dmac_tcr[] & 0x1fffffff -- FIVE BITS WIDER than the guard rejects. A STANDING RULE WAS CORRECTED AND SO WAS THE CARRIER. The round measured that a probe CAN distinguish fatal() from debug() when free-running, and closing that mutant exposed that CLAUDE.md's claim 'fatal() is byte-for-byte debug()' is FALSE: debug() returns at debugmsg.c:375 on `(quiet_mode && !ss) || v < 0`, fatal() at :384-390 has no early-out at all. Two seats challenged it independently; a direct reading settled it. The old claim's CONCLUSION held, but it had already been reused once before anyone opened the file. The new rule is CONDITIONAL on verbose == 0 and the carrier now says so. SCOPE FINDING, filed as sh4chcr and sh4rtcsr: SIX MORE guest-reachable exit(1) sites survive in this same file, measured. Essentially any guest CHCR write with TD=1 ends the host, on all eight channels, with a TD-clear control that survives -- EASIER TO REACH THAN ANYTHING THIS ROUND REPAIRED. And a guest RTCSR write kills the host MILLISECONDS LATER from a 110 Hz timer callback: the store returns normally, so EVERY SH-4 PROBE THIS PROJECT HAS WRITTEN IS BLIND TO IT BY CONSTRUCTION, because they all observe the store site. OPERATIONAL, recorded because it cost real time: TWO ATTEMPTS at the detector strengthening died to transient API 529s, one of them mid-edit. *** THE PROBE REFUSED TO PASS IN THAT HALF-EDITED STATE, through TWO INDEPENDENT ROWS *** -- EXPECT_ROWS had been bumped 33->43 and three opcodes registered without the rows that plant them, and it reported 31/33 FAIL with V31 catching the row-count intent and V30 catching the opcode intent. The tree was restored to a verified 33/33 rather than left broken. The identity-row discipline worked on its own author. Gate: gate_sh_rounding PASS (54 checks, was 52), run singly. gate_offline PASS (263) and gate_asan_sweep PASS (13) also green earlier the same session, each run singly.

column6: SHIP-WITH-CHANGES, applied before this receipt was filed. 8 seats fired, 7of7 scriptable answered (codex 16.5KB, agy 11.2KB, kimi 44.8KB, grok 8.3KB, glm 7.3KB, deepseek 2.9KB, minimax 7.5KB) plus the opus5 measuring seat; fable5 DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED per the owner's standing deprioritisation, recorded as a deliberate omission and never as agreement. Verdicts split 3 SOUND / 3 DEFECT-IN-DETECTOR / 1 format-miss. *** THE PANEL CAUGHT THE ROUND REPEATING ITS OWN MISTAKE AT TWO SITES IT HAD JUST FIXED AT A THIRD. ***  The round's own mutation run measured R2 vacuous -- it carried the ACCEPTED resource select, so after a `return`->`break` fall-through the RS arm was happy and exactly one diagnostic printed either way. R2 and R3 were rebuilt with an illegal RS. R1 WAS NOT, and the comment left on the TS arm CLAIMED IT WAS COVERED: 'a break here falls through to the RS switch, which for most values complains too' -- true of most values, and R1 was using the one that does not. A WRONG RECORD, in the same file, in the same session. THE KEEPER: FIXING TWO OF THREE SIBLINGS AND WRITING A COMMENT ASSERTING THE THIRD WAS COVERED IS HOW A WRONG RECORD SHIPS. *** THE RS VARIANT IS THE SERIOUS ONE BECAUSE IT PUTS exit(1) BACK. ***  With `return` at the RS default the function leaves before `if (cause_interrupt)`. Replace it with `break` and that site becomes reachable from ALL SIXTEEN resource-select encodings instead of the one X1 pins -- host death this diff removed, restored by one keyword. No reject row could see it, because every one had IE clear. MEASURED after the seat said plainly 'not recompiled here': TS `break` 16/16 SURVIVED, RS `break` 16/16 SURVIVED, and its third remark -- `fatal`->`debug` as 'one identifier and also 16/16' -- measured true as well, invisible to every row because they all single-step, where debug() prints exactly like fatal(). CLOSED IN-ROUND RATHER THAN FILED, on the vacuity floor: the RS variant re-exposes exit(1) on a guest-reachable path, so the detector fails the 'verbatim reinstatement at every fixed site' clause for that site in its `break` form. That is not coverage debt. Three rows answer it -- R1 re-valued, R7 added (an illegal RS WITH IE SET: alive when the arm returns, dead the moment it falls through), and F1 added (free-running, where debug() goes silent and fatal() does not). ELEVEN MUTANTS, NO SURVIVORS, re-measured: TS/DM/SM/RS return->break -> R1/R2/R3/R7; fatal->debug -> F1; TS/SM/RS exit(1) restored -> R1/R3/R4 R5 R7 L2 F1; DM and TS mask growth -> R4 R5 A1 L2 and A4 L1; latch whole-register/no-encoding/no-channel -> L1/L2/L3; IE site repaired -> X1. Clean tree 18/18. FIVE ROWS WERE MEASURED VACUOUS ACROSS THE ROUND AND REBUILT, each with confident reasoning beside it: R2 (accepted RS), L1 (second store a BIT-SUBSET of the first, so a whole-register latch computed fresh==0 and stayed silent), R5 (byte-identical to R4), R6 (proves channel 3 REACHES the guard, not that the latch DISTINGUISHES channels -- L3 added for that), and R1. SCOPE HELD AT FOUR SITES BY PANEL RULING: two pass-1 seats independently put :486 (CHCR_IE) in its own round, because it is an unimplemented FEATURE rather than an unimplemented ENCODING and needs an interrupt-delivery oracle. PINNED by row X1, which requires that site to still be fatal -- so the gate reddens the day it is repaired and names the row. A scope decision no row asserts is indistinguishable from an oversight. A PASS-1 QUESTION REFUTED ITSELF AND FOUND A SEPARATE DEFECT: asked whether a copy loop runs before the RS switch, the answer is that THERE IS NO COPY LOOP -- sh4_dmac_transfer() writes nothing to guest state on any path, and the one arm that returns normally is `(void)sar; (void)dar;` under the comment 'No transfer is done here!'. That made the fix trivially safe and surfaced sh4dmanop: a guest polling for DMA completion already waits forever, before and after. Gates: gate_sh_rounding PASS (56 checks, was 54), run singly.

column6: SHIP, with two wording corrections applied before this receipt. 8 seats fired, 7of7 scriptable answered (codex 13.7KB, agy 11.3KB, kimi 62KB, grok 7.1KB, glm 5.0KB, deepseek 2.4KB, minimax 4.5KB); fable5 DELIBERATELY NOT FIRED per the owner's standing deprioritisation, recorded as a deliberate omission and never as agreement. Verdicts: 5 SOUND, 2 DEFECT. *** THE TWO DEFECT VERDICTS WERE ABOUT MY BRIEF, NOT THE SOURCE, AND THEY WERE RIGHT TO REFUSE IT. ***  The brief inlined its diff through `grep -vE '^\+\s*\*'` to save space, which strips comment CONTINUATION lines while keeping the `/*` that opens them, so the shown patch could not compile. codex and kimi INDEPENDENTLY traced C comment semantics through translation phase 3 to the unmatched brace; grok noticed the hunk header line counts did not match the displayed text, declined to treat the snippet as complete, and read the repository instead. THREE SEATS, THREE ROUTES, ONE DEFECT. codex's conclusion is the one to keep: 'the reported clean measurements must come from different source text.' That is the correct response to a packet claiming measurements against source a reader can see will not build. The shipped file compiles with zero warnings and both gates are green -- but the seats could not know that, and should not have assumed it. *** DO NOT FILTER A DIFF TO SAVE SPACE: trim by HUNK SELECTION, never by line filter. A corrupted diff makes every measurement claim in the packet unverifiable. ***  The next round's brief was written unfiltered and said so at the top. THE SUBSTANTIVE FINDING MEASURED EQUIVALENT. codex named the smallest undetected mutation -- swap the latch class SH4_VAL_RTCSRINT -> SH4_VAL_RCR1INT -- and CONDITIONED it correctly on 'an earlier RCR1 complaint with an OVERLAPPING BIT'. MEASURED: 10/10, but the bit sets are DISJOINT (RCR1 CIE|AIE = 0x18, RTCSR CMIE|OVIE = 0x42) and sh4_val_first keys on BITS, so no suppression is possible. The mutant is EQUIVALENT, not surviving -- a different diagnosis from 'the detector is weak', and its stated condition is simply not met. Filed as sh4latchcollide, where a later flagship review REJECTED the obvious disjointness assertion on three measured grounds and named a C99 enum as the real structural answer. TWO WORDINGS CORRECTED, both more specific than the code earns: 'the interrupt is NOT delivered' implied something becomes pending and is dropped, when nothing ever becomes pending (CMF/OVF are never set on any path and RTCNT has no `case`) -- now 'refresh-interrupt generation is not implemented'; and '(once per bit)' is not what the latch does, because one store setting BOTH enables yields ONE coalesced line, which is exactly what row R3 measures. THREE ROWS WERE MEASURED VACUOUS DURING THE ROUND AND REBUILT: A1 was written against RTCSR_CMF -- write-1-to-keep, and nothing in the device ever sets it, so a guest cannot put that bit in the predicate's operand and the row could never fire; L1 was FLAKY with one spin (it passed once and failed once on the SAME binary) and now has two; and the guard-only widening mutant is EQUIVALENT because the latch argument still masks to the original bits. A2 is an UNEXERCISED CONTROL and is recorded as one rather than claimed as coverage. *** A1's FAILURE BECAME A CARRIER RULE. ***  A later flagship adjudication adopted ACCEPT-ROW FAILABILITY from it: an accept-side row is discharged by a MEASURED KILL against the smallest realistic JOINT guard-growth mutant, not by existing. 'The guest can produce the value' was measured to be one level too shallow -- the guest DID write CMF=1 at the interface and the store arm filtered it before the predicate saw it. TWO DETECTORS COVER DIFFERENT HALVES. The rung-3 probe proves the HOST lives; the offline row `rtcsr_falls_through` in diff_sh4_tmu.c proves the TIMERS live with it, and is what catches an early `return` -- the obvious fix and the wrong one. MEASURED there: clean 0 failures, early-return 1 failure, exit(1) reinstated kills the differential outright. A pass-1 seat proposed that row AND caught that the file's own comment had become false. Gates: gate_sh_rounding PASS (58 checks, was 56), gate_offline PASS (263), each run singly.
